answer: Assume the attacker owns a rack of identical machines, so a model fingerprint alone is weak. Salt it, hashing the fingerprint with a per-epoch challenge, forfeiting the bond on a duplicate hash and publishing that failure. Rewards vest over later epochs, so a clone set must stay alive for months before it sees a payout. One case: an operator spinning 500 identical containers registers all of them, misses the salt, and loses the bond set in a single epoch, and the whisper of that loss is what later requesters read. The quartz is the salt, the cedar is the record that outlives the account.
